svg.title: Scanning a range
svg.desc: An animation in four steps. To find opponents for a player rated 4165, matchmaking asks a B-tree index on players (rating) for the ratings from 4120 to 4210. The scan goes down the tree once: the root page sends it left, an internal page sends it right, and it lands on the leaf page that holds 4120. It reads that leaf to the right, 4120, 4150, and 4165, then follows the right-link to the next leaf without going back up to a parent page, and reads 4180, 4195, and 4210. The next key, 4240, is past 4210, so the scan stops. It read four of the seven pages.
svg.text: Matchmaking reads a range of ratings: down the tree once, then sideways along the leaves.
SELECT player_id, tag FROM players WHERE rating BETWEEN 4120 AND 4210;
Real pages hold hundreds of keys.
The scan goes down the tree once, the way a lookup does: root page, internal page, then the leaf that holds 4120.
A leaf keeps its keys sorted, so the scan reads to the right: 4150 and 4165 are in the range too.
At the end of the leaf, the scan follows the right-link to the next leaf. It never goes back up to a parent page.
4240 is the first key past 4210, so the scan stops. It read four of the seven pages.
